notes.visual: A freestanding solid specimen with thin alternating relief bands, folded across several faces; erosion notches and a small rough crosscut cap break up the earlier bellows look, and the band relief survives clay. The overall layer rhythm is still pronounced and regular-looking at 512 px, so retain the narrow BIF claim and do not imply annual increments.
notes.factual: Alternating iron-rich/silica-rich laminae are supported by the actual USGS-hosted James St.John Soudan photo and source text. That photo has specific CC BY 2.0 attribution, not blanket USGS public-domain treatment. Australian Museum DR.19296 text was read but its pixels were not inspected (403); USGS-hosted photo is the disclosed substitute. No annual cadence, exact site/specimen, formation age, sole mechanism, or museum dimension is asserted.
notes.specification: Final r003 has 32 nonuniform band-pairs / 64 alternating laminae and actual rib/recess geometry. The high-contrast rhythm remains visually simplified; do not rename or describe it as generic sedimentary annual bedding.
